clue.text: Grand, in the manner of festivity

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
the French phrase à la, borrowed into English, means in the manner of

explanation.surface: A grand party is described as being in a festive style.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive celebration or special entertainment, a synonym for festivity.

clue.text: Tolerates biased rambling

indicators.note: rambling describes something wandering about aimlessly, so the letters of the neighbouring word wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with prejudiced, wandering talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something is to put up with or endure it, a synonym of tolerate.

clue.text: Boss appearing in the advertisement

indicators.note: the letters wanted show up inside the run of words that follows, across the join of its two words

explanation.surface: The company chief turns up in a commercial.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of an organisation is its chief or leader, a synonym of boss.

clue.text: An upset you finally might get on the briny?

definitions.text: An upset you finally might get on the briny?

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, so the letters before it are tipped into a new order
finally points to the closing letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the briny is an old informal name for the sea

explanation.surface: A question about the queasy stomach a sea voyage can bring on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges AN plus U (the end of 'you') into NAU. The whole clue also defines: seasickness is exactly the upset you might get on the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is the sick, queasy feeling of seasickness, a stomach upset common on boats.

clue.text: What may move our case (last bit of travel)?

definitions.text: What may move our case (last bit of travel)?

indicators.note: to move something is to shift it about, so the letters of the words after it are rearranged
the last bit of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A question about what carries a suitcase at the end of a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' rearranges OUR CASE plus L (the end of 'travel'). The whole clue also defines: at the airport the baggage belt moves your case as the last stage of travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A baggage carousel is the rotating belt that delivers luggage to passengers after a flight.

clue.text: Put pitch on the outside of shed, using a particular tool

indicators.note: one word is placed around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to pitch a ball is to throw or sling it
a hovel is a rough shed or shack

explanation.surface: An instruction to coat the outside of a garden shed with tar, using some tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like the tar but is a verb meaning throw; 'Put' only links, and 'on the outside of' wraps the throw word round the shed word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shovelling means moving material with a shovel, so it is working with one specific tool.

clue.text: Pointed comment by squire finally — hint to provide party food

parts.note: a barb is a sharp, wounding remark

indicators.note: finally signals the last letter of the word squire

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or hint

explanation.surface: A country gentleman makes a sharp remark hinting that he should lay on food for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To barbecue is to cook food outdoors over a grill, typically for a social gathering.

clue.text: Material at bottom of river is mostly hardened clay

indicators.note: in a down entry the second piece sits beneath the first

parts.note: the Cam is the river that flows through Cambridge

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: a brick is a block of fired, hardened clay

explanation.surface: A description of fabric lying on a riverbed beside baked clay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at bottom of' places BRIC under CAM in this down light; the Cam is the river through Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambric is a fine, dense linen or cotton fabric, so it is a type of cloth.

clue.text: Lack of interest in a course leading to the unknown

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come before the one that follows

parts.note: a path is a course or route
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities, so y is an unknown

explanation.surface: Indifference to a course of study that leads nowhere known.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is indifference, an absence of enthusiasm or concern.

clue.text: Uncontrolled or organised party attracting thousand?

parts.note: to run an event is to organise it, past tense ran
a do is an informal word for a party
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Asks whether a big party was chaotic or well arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' looks like the opposite of the definition but supplies RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Random means haphazard, happening without method or control.

clue.text: Hellish situation — love's going wrong — collapse emotionally

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, the realm of the dead, and the city of hell in Dante

indicators.note: going wrong suggests things falling into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word with its s read as letters

explanation.surface: A romance falls apart in hellish fashion and someone breaks down.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissolve, as in dissolve into tears, is to lose emotional control and break down.

clue.text: First opportunity for panto actor to get into gear?

definitions.text: First opportunity for panto actor to get into gear?

parts.words: First opportunity for panto actor to get into gear?
parts.note: gear here means costume, and the first chance to perform in full costume is a run-through before opening night

explanation.surface: Seems to ask when a pantomime performer first gets going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get into gear' suggests starting up, but means putting on the costume; panto is pantomime, a British Christmas stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: The final rehearsal performed in full costume before opening is when actors first wear their outfits.

clue.text: Takes back city area with feeling of delight beginning to spread around

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: rapture is intense joy or delight
EC is the postcode district of the City of London

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An army retakes urban ground as joy begins to spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'city area' is the City of London's postcode district; 'around' puts the joy word round it, and 'beginning to' takes the first letter of 'spread'.
explanation.definitionFit: To recapture something is to seize or regain it, so it means taking back.

clue.text: Arab maybe sounding croaky

indicators.note: sounding signals that the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: a croaky voice is a rough, husky one

explanation.surface: Describes an Arab with a rough voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' seems to be a person but is the breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arab, or Arabian, is a breed of riding animal, so it is an example; 'maybe' marks it.

clue.text: Missile starts to seem costly — unwanted deterrent?

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A rocket looks like an expensive deterrent nobody wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scud is a Soviet-designed ballistic rocket, used in the Gulf War.

clue.text: False belief has us taken in by priest — academic holds that

indicators.note: holds means the word contains what follows

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

indicators.note: one piece is swallowed by the next one named

parts.note: Eli is the priest of the Bible who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A priest and a lecturer combine to fool us with a mistaken idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers: 'taken in by' puts 'us' inside the priest, and 'holds' puts that inside the academic. Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A delusion is a firmly held belief that is untrue, a mistaken conviction.

clue.text: Worried and frightened leader getting put off

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: scared means frightened

explanation.surface: A boss is anxious and nervous after being postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: To have cared about something is to have been concerned or anxious about it.

clue.text: Relaxation of French and English outside temporary accommodation

indicators.note: the first pieces go around the next one

parts.note: de is the French word for of
a tent is a shelter put up for a short stay

explanation.surface: Camping with French and English people sounds restful.
explanation.walkthrough: DE and E go outside TENT, giving DE + TENT + E.
explanation.definitionFit: Détente is an easing of tension, especially between nations, so a relaxation of hostility.

clue.text: Set out to give help to learner

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to assist a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set out' looks like setting off, but means arranged, as a table is laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid, as in a table laid for dinner, means arranged or placed in position.

clue.text: Exercise influence to withdraw an orchestral section

definitions.meaning: to control events secretly from behind the scenes, like a puppeteer
read literally: draw out the violins, violas, cellos and basses

explanation.surface: Wielding power by pulling a section of the orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppeteer works marionettes with cords, so the idiom means controlling things covertly.

clue.text: Getting properly organised, I tried to be less messy

indicators.note: being put in proper order signals the letters being arranged anew

explanation.surface: Someone getting their act together tried to be neater.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidier is the comparative of tidy, meaning neater, more in order.

clue.text: Aim to undermine international plan

indicators.note: in a down entry, to undermine is to sit below the other piece

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A goal of sabotaging a global scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undermine' suggests sabotage, but in this down light it puts END under INT.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend something is to have it in mind as a purpose, so to plan it.

clue.text: Not one of us will change our diets

indicators.note: a promise to alter signals that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stranger will alter what we eat.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider is a person not belonging to a particular group.

clue.text: Play or concert quietly proceeding to end

indicators.note: proceeding to the end means that letter travels to the back of the word

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms
p is the musical marking piano, meaning quietly

explanation.surface: A play or concert is performed softly through to the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a famous London summer concert series.
explanation.definitionFit: To romp is to play boisterously, and a romp is lively play.

clue.text: Bug in weed

definitions.meaning: to bug someone is to annoy or irritate them

explanation.surface: An insect is found in a weed.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means irritate; as a noun it names a stinging plant regarded as a weed.

clue.text: This clue is a sort of model

definitions.meaning: this is the final clue in the puzzle's list
a shoemaker's foot-shaped form on which shoes are made

explanation.surface: The clue claims to be a kind of model.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the final clue, and a cobbler's wooden foot-shaped block bears the same name.

clue.text: Get away and pray sixty minutes after midnight?

parts.note: to pray someone is to beg or implore them
an hour after midnight is one o'clock

explanation.surface: Someone escapes and prays an hour after midnight.
explanation.definitionFit: Begone is an old command meaning go away, a dismissal.

clue.text: After strike, seek men's submission

indicators.note: after being struck, the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: After a walkout, management looks for workers to give in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action but signals the letters of SEEK MEN'S being knocked about.
explanation.definitionFit: Meekness is a quiet, humble willingness to yield, so a submissive attitude.
